title: The point category over one scheme support
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $s\in S$, and let $i_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be the canonical residue-field morphism [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For any scheme $A$, write $\operatorname{Pt}(A_{\mathrm{Et}})$ for the category of geometric morphisms $\mathbf{Set}\to A_{\mathrm{Et}}$, with $2$-morphisms given by natural transformations of direct-image functors [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-trf-geometric-morphism]. The support of a point is the underlying scheme point of any of its geometric representatives [def-weil-geometric-point, lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric]. Postcomposition with $(i_s)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ induces a functor
$$\operatorname{Pt}((\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s))_{\mathrm{Et}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pt}(S_{\mathrm{Et}})$$
which is fully faithful (bijective on every Hom-set) and has as essential image exactly the full subcategory of points supported at $s$. This full subcategory is a connected groupoid: any two of its objects are isomorphic, and all its morphisms are invertible. In particular an automorphism of a geometric point supported at $s$, considered as a point of $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, lifts uniquely to an automorphism of its residue-field point. All fields and topoi may be taken in one common enlarged universe [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Agent-formulated point-category auxiliary for the fixed-support reduction of Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.2; based on Tag 04HU (lemma-points-small-etale-site), Tag 04FN (remark-map-stalks), and Section section-specialization. These sources give geometric representatives and neighbourhood/stalk morphisms; the full-faithfulness formulation is an agent lemma, not quoted as the literal statement of a tag.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric], every point of S_Et is represented by a geometric point x̄:Spec Ω→S, and its inverse image is the geometric stalk colimit. For two such representatives, [lem-trf-etale-point-morphism-classification] identifies 2-morphisms of the associated topos points with the unique morphisms of geometric points over S; [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-morphism-stalk-bijection] supplies the bijectivity of the induced stalk maps. Thus the point category may be computed using geometric representatives and their field maps.

If x̄ lies over s, its structure map factors through the canonical residue-field point i_s:Spec κ(s)→S: the map κ(s)→Ω induced by the geometric point gives Spec Ω→Spec κ(s), and composition with i_s is x̄. Conversely every geometric point obtained by postcomposition with i_s has underlying support s. Therefore the postcomposition functor has essential image exactly the points supported at s.

source.place: Definition 04FS (geometric point over s) and Lemma 04HU

proof.text: For two residue-field points, a 2-morphism after postcomposition with i_s is, by Step 1 and the morphism-classification statement, exactly the same field morphism over κ(s) as the corresponding 2-morphism before postcomposition. Composition with i_s does not change the pointed étale-neighbourhood functor: a neighbourhood of Spec κ(s) is sent to the same étale S-scheme with the composed geometric lift. Hence the induced map on every Hom-set is bijective, so postcomposition is fully faithful.

Given any two objects in the support-s fibre subcategory, factor geometric representatives through i_s by Step 2. The common-extension lemma [lem-trf-family-common-extension-field] embeds their two algebraically closed residue fields over κ(s) into one field K. Choosing an algebraic closure of K gives a geometric point whose stalk point receives morphisms from both representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-morphism-stalk-bijection] these induce invertible 2-morphisms, so the two original objects are isomorphic. The same argument with one object on both sides shows every endomorphism is invertible; Step 3 gives the unique lift of each automorphism to the residue-field point.
